events.what_it_is: A Climate Week NYC festival of eco-inspired performances, installations, visual art and hands-on workshops at the Climate Imaginarium on Governors Island.
events.what_is_free: Festival admission, performances, visual-art exhibitions and interactive activities are free. The registration page suggests a $10 donation but says tickets are free and no one will be turned away for lack of funds.
events.caveats: Official and organizer sources describe the festival as free and open to the public. Reservations are recommended, not stated as required. The Luma page shows a suggested $10 pay-what-you-want donation, but explicitly says tickets are free. Governors Island ferry transportation may require a separate fare depending on route/time and rider eligibility.
events.practical_notes: Interactive activities, workshops and visual art run 11 AM–4 PM; performances run 12:45–2:45 PM. Climate Imaginarium is Building 406A on Colonels Row. Ferry transportation is separate from event admission.

events.event_name: The Art of Change: Realigning our Relationship with Nature
events.what_it_is: A public participatory Climate Week NYC opening ceremony combining workshops, performance, sound installation, painting, poetry, a climate commemoration and community gathering.
events.what_is_free: The program is available on a pay-what-you-want ticket with a suggested $10 donation; the host says no one will be turned away due to lack of funds. Lunch is provided, with a study session available for attendees fasting for Yom Kippur.
events.caveats: The ticket page instructs visitors to get a ticket to join. Admission is pay-what-you-want with a suggested $10 donation; the host states no one will be turned away due to lack of funds. Governors Island ferry transportation may require a separate fare depending on route/time and rider eligibility.
events.practical_notes: 11 AM–1 PM workshops and performances; 1–2 PM lunch/study session; 2–4 PM climate commemoration; 4–5 PM closing. Climate Imaginarium is Building 406A on Colonels Row.

occurrences.details: Free and open to the public; reservations recommended. Performances run 12:45–2:45 PM within the 11 AM–4 PM festival window.
Free/pay-what-you-want ticket registration is open; suggested donation is $10 and the host states no one will be turned away due to lack of funds.
